groups.title: Directories of certified reading specialists
groups.intro: Search these official lists to find people trained in proven methods for dyslexia, such as Structured Literacy and Orton-Gillingham. Each provider sets their own prices.

groups.title: Free and low-cost tutoring programs
groups.intro: Nonprofit programs that tutor students for free or at minimal cost. Some have waitlists or only serve certain areas.

groups.title: Learning centers and online programs
groups.intro: Paid programs with their own teaching methods, in person or online.

groups.title: General tutoring sites
groups.intro: Large sites where you browse and hire tutors yourself. Tutors are not checked for dyslexia training, so use the checklist below.

groups.title: Free practice on your own
groups.intro: Free lessons you can use any time, alongside a tutor or on your own.

sites.name: IDA Provider Directory
sites.what: A directory of IDA member professionals who offer tutoring, reading instruction, assessment, educational therapy, speech-language therapy, advocacy, and more.
sites.how: Search by service and location, then contact providers directly.
sites.cost_label: Free to search · providers set fees
sites.note: IDA says listings are not an endorsement, so check credentials yourself.

sites.name: CERI: Find a Structured Literacy Professional
sites.org: Center for Effective Reading Instruction (linked from IDA)
sites.what: A directory of professionals certified in Structured Literacy, the teaching approach IDA recommends for dyslexia.
sites.how: Find a certified professional near you or online, then contact them directly.
sites.cost_label: Free to search · providers set fees

sites.name: Wilson Reading System: Find a Certified Instructor
sites.what: A map of currently credentialed Wilson Dyslexia Practitioners and Therapists.
sites.how: Click your area on the map to see certified instructors.
sites.cost_label: Free to search · instructors set fees
sites.note: Wilson lists only people whose credentials are current.

sites.name: ALTA: Certified Academic Language Therapists
sites.what: ALTA certifies academic language therapists who provide evidence-based dyslexia therapy.
sites.how: Use ALTA's site to find a certified therapist near you.
sites.cost_label: Free to search · therapists set fees

sites.name: Barton Reading & Spelling: Tutors
sites.what: Find a Certified Barton Tutor locally or online, or have a trusted adult (like a relative) pass Barton's tutor screening and tutor at home with the program.
sites.how: Look up certified tutors in your area, or follow the steps to tutor your own student.
sites.cost_label: Tutors set fees · program materials sold separately

sites.name: ASHA ProFind
sites.what: Find from over 20,000 ASHA-certified speech-language pathologists who are accepting referrals. They can help with spoken and written language difficulties.
sites.cost_label: Free to search · providers set fees

sites.name: Children's Dyslexia Centers
sites.what: One-on-one tutoring for grades 1–12, twice a week after school (about 55 minutes), using a structured language approach. More than 40 centers in 13 states.
sites.how: Find a center in your state and contact it to apply.

sites.name: New Haven Reads
sites.what: Free one-on-one literacy tutoring for any student struggling with reading in grades 1–12, at least one hour a week, at four New Haven locations.
sites.how: Fill out the waitlist application on their site (also available in Spanish).

sites.name: Reading Partners
sites.what: Twice-weekly one-on-one reading tutoring for elementary students in partner schools, using a phonics-based approach.
sites.how: Ask your child's school if it partners with Reading Partners.

sites.name: ProLiteracy
sites.what: A leading adult literacy organization that supports reading programs for adults across the U.S.
sites.how: Use their site to find adult literacy programs and resources.

sites.name: Lindamood-Bell Learning Centers
sites.what: Reading and comprehension instruction at learning centers and through an online academy. It starts with a learning ability evaluation.
sites.how: Find a center near you, or ask about the online academy.

sites.name: Wyzant
sites.what: Browse private tutors in 300+ subjects and compare ratings.
sites.how: Search for “reading” or “dyslexia,” then interview tutors using the checklist below.
sites.cost_label: Paid · each tutor sets a rate

sites.name: Varsity Tutors
sites.what: Private and group tutoring, classes, and test prep online in 3,000+ subjects.
sites.how: Request a reading tutor and ask about their training with dyslexia.

sites.name: Outschool
sites.what: Live online classes for kids ages 3–18 in a huge range of subjects.
sites.how: Search for reading or dyslexia classes and read the teacher's profile.

sites.name: Khan Academy
sites.what: Free online lessons and practice in many school subjects.
sites.how: Create a free account and pick a course at your level.

items: Ask about their training in methods made for dyslexia, like Structured Literacy or Orton-Gillingham.
Ask which program certified them, what level they finished, and when.
Ask for references from other parents, students, or professionals.
Ask how they set goals and measure progress.
Meet first. Make sure the tutor is a good fit, and that they work with your age group.
Ask to see their background check and child abuse clearance.
Remember: being listed in a directory doesn't mean a tutor is recommended. You make the final choice.
